hypothesis: On every embedded subgroup of the six fixed small p-groups, a shortest normal-cyclic chain calculation agrees with an independently organized exhaustive-chain and coset-quotient calculation. The metadata preserves at least one known same-abstract-subgroup embedding distinction and corrects at least one log-index surrogate. The older elementary-quotient lower bound is retained as a bound rather than silently labeled exact. All chain witnesses and a deterministic change of element labels validate exactly.

input.kind: synthetic exact combinatorial metadata audit for an equivariant topology knowledge graph; not a spectral computation
input.source_locator: Family314 introduction: definition of ell, C_(p^2) x C_p embedding example, D8 noncentral order-two example and old lower/upper bounds
input.exposure: Full source and selected older statements already read. The C4xC2 embedding distinction, cyclic-order-four loss and D8 lower-bound gap are known controls stated or reasoned about before this registration. This is nonblind metadata calibration, not a newly discovered theorem or a new algorithm.

groups.name: UT3F3
groups.elements: triples (a,b,c) in{0,1,2}^3 representing upper unitriangular3x3 F3 matrices

input.subgroups: Every subgroup of each fixed group, retaining its actual embedded element set. Verify group axioms on the complete multiplication tables before use.
input.subgroup_inventory_a: Start at identity subgroup and repeatedly adjoin each group element using multiplication-closure saturation until no new subgroup appears.
input.subgroup_inventory_b: Enumerate all generating subsets of at most log_p(|G|) elements, using an independently organized generator-action orbit closure. Every strictly increasing subgroup chain in these p-groups has at most log_p(|G|) steps, which establishes this generator-count sufficiency.
input.relabeling: Apply the deterministic element permutation old index i -> |G|-1-i, moving the identity too; rebuild tables and embedded sets and compare all ell values. No random selection or post-result fixture expansion.

baseline: Compute log_p[G:H] as an intentionally invalid general exact-loss surrogate. For the old lower bound, quotient by the normal closure of H, all commutators and all pth powers and take the logarithm of the quotient order; retain this only as elementary-quotient rank. A key using only abstract cyclic order-two subgroup type conflates the known C4xC2 embeddings H1=<(2,0)> and H2=<(0,1)>.
judge: MethodA uses normality and existence of an element whose powers together with the lower subgroup generate the upper subgroup, then shortest paths through the subgroup lattice. MethodB explicitly constructs cosets and tests quotient cyclicity, enumerates every strict subgroup chain and minimizes its valid length. Check every returned witness against MethodB. Independently validate the two complete subgroup inventories, quotient controls and element relabeling. Neither method evaluates Morava homology or assumes r_n=ell to determine ell.
failure: Any group-axiom failure, incomplete or differing subgroup inventory, oracle disagreement, invalid witness, relabeling failure, failed fixed control or absence of the declared surrogate mismatch. Retain all failures and exact payloads; do not replace groups or thresholds after outputs.
metrics: shortest chain and witness for every embedded subgroup
limits: This tests exact finite-group metadata and a knowledge-graph mapping, not the new spectral sharpness theorem or finite genuine-spectrum nonvanishing. Abelian and D8 controls are already treated by older results. No claim of a faster group algorithm, independent provider review, mathematical human review or engineering deployment. Finite tests cannot establish the universal identity r_n=ell or general height independence. Results are exact integers and embedded sets, so no floating-point tolerance or statistical extrapolation is used.
